hints.title: Think of airports as vertices
hints.body: The tickets are directed edges. Using every edge exactly once is an Eulerian trail problem, not a shortest-path problem.

hints.title: Build the trail backwards
hints.body: A depth-first walk that keeps taking available edges until it gets stuck records airports in reverse order. Reversing that record produces a valid Eulerian trail.

hints.title: Control the tie-breaking
hints.body: Sort each airport's outgoing destinations so the smallest one is taken first. Using a stack or a descending list that is popped from the end avoids repeatedly removing from the front.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
for each ticket in descending lexicographic order:
    append destination to graph[source]
route = []
visit(airport):
    while graph[airport] is not empty:
        visit(pop last destination)
    route.append(airport)
visit("JFK")
reverse route
return route
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete implementation.
